messages:
maria: FYI getting paged a lot last night for very short GPU node flaps in eu-west1 (30-90s). Most incidents auto-recover and are noisy for oncall. thinking: convert most of these to ticket-only unless sustained.

ton y: saw that too — ~40 pages between 00:30-03:00. oncall was overwhelmed.

jen: +1. Are these preemptions/spot reclaiming? If so we should be careful not to suppress real capacity failures.

maria: yeah mostly spot/preemptions on non-prod pools and some dev-dedicated. proposal: page only if error spike is sustained across 5m AND affects >X pods or >Y requests. otherwise create ticket.

dev-sre: we can implement with a `for: 5m` and add a `sum_over_time` guard. also group by `pool` and `region` at alertmanager so one page per-owner.

maria: rough alert rule draft below — open to edits:

```yaml
- alert: GPUNodeFlap_SustainedErrors
  expr: |
    sum by (pool,region) (increase(gpu_node_error_total[5m])) > 10
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "Sustained GPU node errors in {{ $labels.pool }} ({{ $labels.region }})"

- alert: GPUNodeFlap_Spike
  expr: |
    sum by (pool,region) (increase(gpu_node_error_total[1m])) > 3
  for: 0m
  labels:
    severity: ticket
  annotations:
    summary: "Transient GPU node error spike in {{ $labels.pool }} ({{ $labels.region }})"
```

tony: I like separating spike vs sustained. For non-prod pools we should lower thresholds and route to ticket-only by default.

jen: can we also add a route in alertmanager that silences `ticket` alerts during our maintenance window (00:00-06:00) for non-prod? keep pages for prod.

dev-sre: yep — alertmanager route pseudocode: group_by: [pool, region], match_re: pool =~ "^(prod-).*" -> page receiver, else -> ticket receiver. and a mute schedule for non-prod night window.

ops-bot: Grafana panel updated: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/gpu-flares — added series for pages vs tickets last 7d.

maria: next steps: 1) jen opens alertmanager route PR 2) tony will own the 72h experiment (apply new rules in staging then prod) 3) dev-sre to add grouping labels and test dedupe 4) add SLO panel comparing page-rate vs error-rate.

tony: will take experiment. plan: enable new rules in eu-west1 canary first, monitor pages for 72h, then roll global if good.

jen: I'll draft the PR and include the mute schedule, plus a runbook blurb for oncall to explain ticket vs page thresholds.

maria: good. also put a note in console alerting docs and link the grafana panel. thanks all :thumbsup:

tony: quick question — what values for X/Y on the rule? think starting with >10 errors over 5m and >20% of pool membership failing might be sensible.

maria: agree. start conservative: 10 errors / 5m OR failure_ratio > 0.2. we can tune after experiment.

dev-sre: I'll add both checks to the expr: `increase(...) > 10 or (sum(failed{...}) / sum(total{...}) > 0.2)` and push tests.

maria: perfect. tagging follow-ups in the ticket I'm about to create. experiment kickoff tomorrow morning.

ops-bot: Created ticket REDWOOD-OPS-4381: "Experiment: tiered paging/ticketing for GPU flares (eu-west1)" assigned to tony.

maria: thanks — will monitor and close loop after 72h. :rocket:
